problem: The sentence 'Every request is rounded up to B bytes' is imprecise. A request larger than one block (say 200 bytes with B = 128) is rounded up to a whole number of blocks, not to B bytes. The worked example only uses requests ≤ B, so the wording is never corrected.
fix: Every request is rounded up to a whole number of blocks, that is, to a multiple of B bytes; a 100-byte request from 128-byte blocks fits in one block and uses 128 bytes, while a 200-byte request needs two blocks.

problem: '.bss (zero-initialised globals)' leaves out static variables. The line above correctly says .data holds 'initialised globals and static variables', but a zero-initialised static variable (for example a static buffer) also lives in .bss, and a student may write otherwise in an exam.

The figure stacks flash, .data/.bss, heap, free RAM and stack on one continuous ramp labelled 'low address' to 'high address'. On most microcontrollers flash and RAM sit in separate address ranges with a gap between them, so a student can wrongly conclude that .data follows code contiguously in one address space.
fix: Keep the ramp but add a note that it shows the linked image layout, and that on most microcontrollers flash and RAM occupy separate address ranges.
